MUJAHID:v1p316#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p316#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p316#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says Joseph asked the released prisoner to mention him to the king; the prisoner forgot until the king dreamed. Satan made Joseph forget remembrance of his Lord and direct his plea to the king, so Joseph remained imprisoned for years because he had said to mention him to the king.

MUJAHID:v1p317#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p317#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p317#2/r1.claim: Mujahid defines bid' as a span of three to nine years.

MUQATIL:12:41-42/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r3.claim: Joseph asked the cupbearer to mention him to the king, but Satan made Joseph forget to ask God; God kept him imprisoned as punishment for relying on the king.

MUQATIL:12:41-42/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r4.claim: Joseph served seven years before the incident and five more years as punishment, totaling twelve years; the additional years fulfill 12:35.

MUQATIL:12:41-42/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r5.claim: The Prophet said Joseph would have left prison that very day had he called upon God rather than seeking help from the king.

MUQATIL:12:41-42/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r6.claim: Gabriel rebuked Joseph for relying on a servant after God had made him beloved to his father and protected him from sin; Joseph prayed for forgiveness through his forefathers.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r1.claim: The Prophet said Joseph would not have remained imprisoned so long had he not asked the cupbearer to mention him to his master.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r2.claim: Qatada reports that Joseph remained imprisoned for seven years.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r3.claim: Wahb says Job suffered for seven years, Joseph stayed imprisoned seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was punished among beasts for seven years.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323#2/r4.claim: The Prophet admired Joseph's patience and generosity: he interpreted the king's dream before seeking release, then sought vindication before leaving prison; his earlier plea prolonged his stay.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#4/r1.claim: Rabbika means “your master,” not Lord in the divine sense.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#4/r2.speaker: الأعشى
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#4/r2.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line addresses a generous king as rabb, attesting the meaning “master.”

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#4/r3.claim: Biḍʿ means one to nine; Abū ʿUbayda narrows it to one through four, below half a decade.

TUSTARI:12:42/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:12:42/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:12:42/r1.claim: A report says Gabriel visited Joseph in prison, conveyed God’s rebuke for seeking an intermediary, and foretold years more in prison; when Joseph learned God was pleased with him, he was unconcerned.

TUSTARI:12:42/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:12:42/r2.speaker: علي ابن أبي طالب
TUSTARI:12:42/r2.claim: Ali compared disciplining his own soul to a shepherd who gathers his flock on one side only for it to scatter on another.

TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r1.claim: Yusuf knew the surviving cupbearer would be saved and asked him to tell his master of Yusuf's unjust imprisonment without a crime; rabb means the king or master.

TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r2.claim: Qatada understands the word ظن as uncertainty, since dream interpretation involves conjecture; al-Tabari rejects this application to Yusuf.

TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r3.claim: Al-Tabari rejects reading Yusuf's prediction as conjecture: prophets cannot give a definite report that might prove false without undermining the proof of their message; Yusuf's firm prediction shows he knew it would occur.

TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
TAB-FULL:v13p169#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi reports that a companion at the prison door asked what to convey, and Yusuf asked to be remembered before his master, the king.

TAB-FULL:v13p176#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p176#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p176#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says Yusuf was not mentioned to the king until the king's dream; Satan made Yusuf forget his Lord and seek relief from the king, so he remained imprisoned as punishment.

TAB-FULL:v13p176#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p176#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p176#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq instead says Satan made the cupbearer forget to tell the king about Yusuf; Yusuf's imprisonment then continued as punishment for asking the cupbearer to remember him.

TAB-FULL:v13p176#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p176#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p176#2/r3.claim: Qatada and Wahb report a seven-year prison term; Wahb lists it alongside Job's seven-year affliction and Nebuchadnezzar's seven years among beasts.

TAB-FULL:v13p176/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r1.claim: Al-Tabari reads Satan's causing forgetfulness as a lapse in Yusuf, who forgot to appeal to God; this lengthened his confinement and was painful punishment.

TAB-FULL:v13p176/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r2.speaker: مالك بن دينار
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r2.claim: Malik ibn Dinar reports a divine reproach to Yusuf for taking an intermediary besides God, followed by Yusuf's lament that affliction had distracted his heart.

TAB-FULL:v13p176/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r3.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r3.claim: Several reports attributed to the Prophet say Yusuf's request that the cupbearer remember him caused him to remain in prison longer; Hasan wept and applied the lesson to people who turn to others in hardship.

TAB-FULL:v13p176/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits a Prophetic report that Yusuf would not have remained so long had he not sought relief from someone besides God.

TAB-FULL:v13p176/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p176/r5.claim: Qatada reports a Prophetic saying that Yusuf's seeking intercession through the cupbearer prolonged his imprisonment as a punishment.

TAB-FULL:v13p177/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the duration of bid' here was seven years, matching Yusuf's prison term.

TAB-FULL:v13p177/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r2.claim: Qatada defines bid' as three to nine years.

TAB-FULL:v13p177/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r3.claim: Mujahid likewise defines bid' as three to nine years.

TAB-FULL:v13p177/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas defines bid' as fewer than ten years.

TAB-FULL:v13p177/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r5.speaker: الفراء
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r5.claim: Al-Farra says bid' is used with tens, from ten through ninety, as an odd number within that range, but not with a hundred or thousand.

TAB-FULL:v13p177/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p177/r6.claim: Al-Tabari holds bid' ranges from three to nine and is never below three, following observed Arabic usage.

ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r2.claim: ‘Mention me to your lord’ means mention Joseph to the man’s master, the king.

ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r3.claim: Satan caused Joseph to forget mentioning God.

ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r4.speaker: قال بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r4.claim: Some define biḍʿ as three to five years; Quṭrub extends it to seven; al-Aṣmaʿī, which the author calls correct, says three to nine.

ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī derives biḍʿ from cutting off a piece and says it denotes a part of a number below ten, from three through nine.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r1.claim: The Prophet prayed for God's mercy on Joseph and said that, had Joseph not asked to be remembered by his master, he would not have remained imprisoned so long.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r2.claim: Hasan also attributes this saying to the Prophet, then weeps that people turn to others when trouble comes.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r3.claim: Joseph asked the prisoner who would be freed to mention him to the king, but the man did not do so until the king saw his dream.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r4.claim: Joseph asked the king to be told of his unjust imprisonment.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r5.speaker: مالك بن دينار
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r5.claim: Hasan reports a rebuke to Joseph for relying on an intermediary; Joseph answered that distress had overwhelmed him and words escaped his tongue, and he wept.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r6.claim: The cupbearer forgot the king whom Joseph had asked him to remember.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r7.speaker: ابن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148#2/r7.claim: After the cupbearer returned to his post and regained his master's favor, he forgot the king Joseph had asked him to mention, and Joseph remained imprisoned for years.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r1.speaker: أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r1.claim: God reminded Joseph of rescue from the pit and his brothers' plot, asking why he forgot God and remembered a human; Joseph blamed anguish and a spoken word, and God kept him imprisoned seven years. A similar report is attributed to al-Thawri.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r2.claim: Joseph was punished three times; the second punishment was prolonged imprisonment for asking the cupbearer to remember him.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r3.claim: “A few years” can mean three to nine years.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r4.claim: One interpretation of “a few years” is twelve years.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r5.speaker: طاوس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2149/r5.claim: Tawus and al-Dahhak give the duration as fourteen years.

THALABI:v5p224/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p224/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says biḍʿ is less than ten; al-Farra says Arabs use it from three through nine with tens, not with hundreds or thousands.

THALABI:v5p224/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r11.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v5p224/r11.claim: Most commentators say Joseph stayed seven years; Wahb compares his imprisonment with seven-year trials of Job and Nebuchadnezzar.

THALABI:v5p224/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p224/r4.claim: Most commentators say Joseph thought the cupbearer would be saved; Qatada takes the thought as uncertain conjecture, but the author prefers the first as more fitting for prophets.

THALABI:v5p224/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p224/r5.claim: Joseph asks the cupbearer to remember him before his master, the king.

THALABI:v5p224/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p224/r6.claim: One interpretation says Satan made Joseph forget his Lord, so he sought relief through a human and remained imprisoned longer; this was a lapse of heedlessness.

THALABI:v5p224/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r7.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
THALABI:v5p224/r7.claim: Ibn Ishaq instead takes the pronoun as referring to the cupbearer: Satan made him forget to mention Joseph to his master.

THALABI:v5p224/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v5p224/r8.claim: Abu Ubayda defines biḍʿ as a number from three to five.

THALABI:v5p224/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r9.speaker: مجاهد والأصمعي
THALABI:v5p224/r9.claim: Mujahid and al-Asmaʿi define biḍʿ as three to nine.

THALABI:v5p225/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p225/r1.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v5p225/r1.claim: Al-Hasan transmits the Prophet’s prayer for mercy on Joseph, saying his request to the cupbearer prolonged the imprisonment; al-Hasan weeps that people likewise turn to others in hardship.

THALABI:v5p225/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p225/r2.speaker: مالك بن دينار
THALABI:v5p225/r2.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says God rebuked Joseph for taking a human as an agent and lengthened his confinement after he asked the cupbearer to remember him.

THALABI:v5p225/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p225/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p225/r3.claim: In a reported encounter, Gabriel tells Joseph that God asks why he sought help from human beings and swears to keep him in prison; Joseph accepts if God is pleased.

THALABI:v5p225/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p225/r4.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v5p225/r4.claim: Kaʿb recounts Gabriel asking Joseph who created, favored, accompanied in the well, rescued, and taught him; Joseph answers God each time and is asked why he appealed to a human.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r1.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r1.claim: Here ظن means that Joseph knew which prisoner would be saved; the wording uses conjecture for knowledge.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r10.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وقطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r10.claim: بضع can mean a number from three through seven.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r11.speaker: مجاهد والأصمعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r11.claim: بضع can mean a number from three through nine.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r12.claim: بضع can mean a number from three through ten.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r13.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r13.claim: A further reported definition makes بضع the interval from three to five.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r14.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r14.claim: Al-Farra says بضع occurs with the tens from ten through ninety, but not after one hundred.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r15.speaker: ابن جريج وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r15.claim: One report says Joseph's whole imprisonment lasted seven years.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas gives Joseph's imprisonment as twelve years.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r17.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r17.claim: Al-Dahhak gives Joseph's imprisonment as fourteen years; the period of punishment may be only part of the whole imprisonment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r18.speaker: وهب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r18.claim: Wahb says Joseph was imprisoned seven years and Job endured affliction for seven years.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r19.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r19.claim: Al-Kalbi says Joseph spent seven years imprisoned after the five years in which he had asked the cupbearer to remember him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r2.claim: Alternatively, Joseph only conjectured that one prisoner would be saved, without certainty.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r3.claim: Joseph spoke conjecturally because dream interpretation itself is conjectural.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r4.claim: Another explanation is that Joseph doubted whether the prisoners had told the truth about their dreams.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r5.claim: Joseph asked the saved cupbearer to mention him to his master, the king al-Walid ibn al-Rayan, hoping to be released.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r6.claim: Satan made the saved prisoner forget to mention Joseph to his master until the king later dreamed.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r7.claim: Alternatively, Satan caused Joseph to forget invoking God and relying on Him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r8.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra through Abu Salama asks God to have mercy on Joseph and says he would not have stayed so long had he not asked the cupbearer to remember him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p39/r9.claim: Joseph was punished with a longer imprisonment for asking the saved prisoner to remember him; had he remembered God, God would have freed him.

QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r10.claim: Joseph was rebuked for asking the prisoner to mention him to the ruler, since he forgot to seek help from God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Muqātil, and most commentators interpret ظن as certainty: يوسف knew the cupbearer would be saved.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r10.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r10.claim: Al-Kalbī takes the pronoun to refer to the cupbearer, whom Satan made forget to mention Joseph to the king.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r11.speaker: ابن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r11.claim: Ibn Isḥāq takes the pronoun to refer to the cupbearer, whom Satan made forget to mention Joseph to the king.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r12.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ records both explanations of whose forgetting is described.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r13.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r13.claim: The grammar favors Joseph as the referent because taking it as the cupbearer requires an omitted phrase, “mention him to his master.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r14.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r14.claim: The counterargument says Joseph could not be punished for forgetfulness; the response is that “forgetting” here means deliberate abandonment, not involuntary lapse.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r2.claim: Qatāda takes ظن as uncertainty: dream interpretation is conjectural, and God may annul or confirm what He wills.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r3.claim: The conjectural reading aligns with the view that Joseph did not make a certain prediction; the text calls the survivor one he supposed would escape.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r4.claim: ربك here means the king, Joseph's master.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r5.claim: Joseph asked the released cupbearer to tell the king that an unjustly imprisoned young man remained in prison.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r6.claim: Mujāhid says Satan made Joseph forget to seek God and caused him to seek help from the king, so he remained in prison.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās shares the view that Satan made Joseph forget to seek his Lord.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj chooses the reading that the pronoun in فأنساه refers to Joseph, whom Satan caused to forget mention of his Lord.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r9.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p121/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the pronoun to refer to the cupbearer: Satan made him forget to mention Joseph to the king.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines bidʿ as below ten and below half of a decade, roughly one through four.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r10.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, Joseph appealed to a creature shortly before release and thereby neglected God, so he remained in prison.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r11.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that the Prophet said Joseph would not have remained so long had he not said “mention me to your master”; al-Ḥasan wept that people likewise turn to others in distress.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r2.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī defines bidʿ as three through nine; al-Zajjāj calls this the correct view, deriving it from “a cut” and a portion of a number.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r3.claim: Qatāda agrees that bidʿ means three to nine.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says bidʿ means three to nine, is used with tens rather than hundreds, and contrasts with نيف for one or two; its feminine is بضعة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r5.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad and a group define bidʿ as the span between two decades, or broadly any number below ten; al-Akhfash gives one to ten.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r6.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash defines bidʿ as any number from one through ten.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r7.speaker: الشعبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reports that the Prophet asked the Companions the range of bidʿ and they answered one to ten; Ibn ʿAbbās shares that view.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r8.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r8.claim: Mujāhid, Quṭrub, and most commentators define bidʿ as three to nine and say Joseph's second imprisonment lasted seven years after an earlier five.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p124/r9.claim: Muqātil reverses the durations: the first period was seven years and the later period five.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r2.claim: Joseph asked the rescued cupbearer to tell the king that an innocent young man was imprisoned; the source says Satan made Joseph forget seeking God's help and led him to seek the king's help instead.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r3.claim: Joseph's reliance on the king instead of God was punished by seven years longer in prison.

JISHUMI:v5p3646/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the span is from three to five.

JISHUMI:v5p3646/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r11.speaker: قتادة والأصمعي
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r11.claim: Qatāda and al-Aṣmaʿī say the span reaches up to nine.

JISHUMI:v5p3646/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r7.claim: Buḍʿ is a piece of time or flesh, and bidāʿa is part of one's property; the word's root suggests cutting off a portion.

JISHUMI:v5p3646/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says buḍʿ denotes a span from three to ten.

JISHUMI:v5p3646/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r9.speaker: الفراء ومجاهد والأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, Mujāhid, and al-Aṣamm say the span reaches up to seven.

JISHUMI:v5p3652/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r1.claim: In hardship one must rely on God as the main support, even though seeking help from another person may be permissible.

JISHUMI:v5p3652/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r2.claim: The cupbearer forgot Joseph despite witnessing miracles and the short interval because royal duties occupied him and he gave little attention to Joseph.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas counts three slips for Joseph: his desire led to prison, asking the cupbearer to remember him prolonged prison, and calling his brothers thieves led them to say his brother had stolen.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r4.claim: Here “thought” means knew; Joseph asks the surviving cupbearer to mention a wrongfully imprisoned youth to his master, the king.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r1.claim: One reading makes Satan cause the cupbearer to forget Joseph when mentioning him to his master; the majority, including Ibn Abbas, say Satan made Joseph forget God when seeking relief through another person.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r10.speaker: كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r10.claim: Kaab reports Gabriel reminding Joseph that God created him, made his father love him, rescued him from the well, taught him dream interpretation, and protected him—so why seek a mortal’s help?

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r2.claim: Joseph’s reliance on another person was a lapse brought on by Satan.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r3.claim: Mujahid defines a few years as anywhere from three to seven.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r4.claim: Qatada defines a few years as anywhere from three to nine.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says a few years means fewer than ten.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r6.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r6.claim: Most commentators say seven years, and that Joseph had already spent five years imprisoned, making twelve in total.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r7.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r7.claim: Wahb gives three seven-year examples: Job’s affliction, Joseph’s prison term, and Nebuchadnezzar’s confinement among beasts.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r8.speaker: مالك بن دينار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r8.claim: Malik ibn Dinar relates that God rebuked Joseph for taking the cupbearer as an intermediary; Joseph wept and promised not to repeat the lapse.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r9.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p244/r9.claim: Al-Hasan recounts Gabriel asking Joseph whether he was ashamed to seek an intercessor among humans; Joseph replies that he does not mind imprisonment if God is pleased with him.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r1.claim: If Yusuf interpreted by reasoning, he was the one who thought the cupbearer would be saved; if he interpreted by revelation, the cupbearer was the one who knew with certainty.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r2.claim: Yusuf asked the cupbearer to describe his case to the king in hopes the king would rescue him.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r3.claim: The Satan caused the cupbearer to forget to mention Yusuf to his master; an alternative says Yusuf forgot God when he entrusted his case to someone else.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r4.claim: Buḍʿ means three to nine years; most reports say Yusuf remained imprisoned seven years.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r5.claim: Satan can prompt forgetfulness by distracting a person, but initiating forgetfulness directly is within God's power alone; the verse links this to abrogation.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r6.claim: The possessive in dhikri rabbihi is licensed by close association with the king, or by ellipsis of the word reports before lord.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r7.claim: Seeking another person's help is generally permissible, supported by verses and reports, including God's help for servants who help one another and relief of a believer's distress.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r8.claim: Though help may be sought even from non-Muslims to repel harm, a prophet's better course is to entrust a trial only to God, especially to avoid unbelievers gloating.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r9.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p445/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan would weep at this verse and say that when trouble comes, people like us turn to other people.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas counts three slips by Joseph: the episode with her, asking the cupbearer to remember him, and accusing the brothers of theft, which prompted the reply about Benjamin.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r10.claim: Qatada takes ẓanna in its ordinary sense because dream interpretation remains conjectural.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r11.claim: The author says Qatada’s reading requires taking Joseph’s قضي الأمر to mean only that his interpretation was finished, not that the future was divinely settled.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r12.claim: Another grammatical reading makes the man who was promised release the subject of ظن: joy elevated him to expect rescue.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r9.claim: Here ẓanna can mean certainty, since Joseph had said the outcome was settled, though it had not yet happened.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r1.claim: Joseph asks the king’s cupbearer to remember him by reporting his knowledge and standing, his wrongful imprisonment, or both.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r10.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r10.claim: Al-Farra says biḍʿ is used with tens but not with hundreds or thousands.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r11.claim: Reports say Joseph had already served five years, then received seven years for asking the cupbearer to remember him; another report gives two additional years.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r12.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r12.claim: Al-Hasan attributes to the Prophet the saying that Joseph would not have remained imprisoned so long if not for his word; Hasan wept and warned that people turn to others when trouble comes.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r2.claim: One explanation makes the pronoun in أنساه refer to Joseph: he forgot to appeal to God and relied on a human; reports say Gabriel reproached him and this prolonged the prison term.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r3.claim: A reported divine address says Joseph took an intermediary besides God and would therefore remain imprisoned longer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq makes the pronoun refer to the cupbearer, who forgot to mention Joseph to his master; رب then means the king.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r5.claim: The most common definition of biḍʿ is three to ten; Ibn Abbas’s definition informs Malik’s rule in claims and oaths.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda says biḍʿ is below a full decade and below half of one, ranging from one to four.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r7.speaker: الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash gives biḍʿ the range one to ten.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r8.claim: Qatada defines biḍʿ as three to nine, supported by a prophetic explanation to Abu Bakr about the Romans’ victory over Persia.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247/r9.claim: Mujahid narrows biḍʿ to three through seven.

TABRISI:12:42/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r1.speaker: أكثرون، الجبائي
TABRISI:12:42/r1.claim: The majority and al-Jubbaʾi take ظن as certain knowledge received by revelation, as in the verse about expecting to meet one's account; this is the author's preferred reading.

TABRISI:12:42/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:42/r10.claim: The lesson is to rely on and seek help from God in hardship, although seeking help from other people is also permissible.

TABRISI:12:42/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:12:42/r2.claim: Qatada takes ظن in its ordinary sense of conjecture, since Yusuf could not verify that the prisoner's dream report was true.

TABRISI:12:42/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:42/r3.claim: Yusuf asked the escaped cupbearer to mention that he was unjustly imprisoned to his master, the king.

TABRISI:12:42/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:42/r4.claim: The author first explains Satan's making Yusuf forget as Yusuf forgetting to mention God and instead asking a human for help, when reliance on God was more fitting.

TABRISI:12:42/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r5.speaker: الحسن، محمد بن إسحاق، الجبائي، أبو مسلم
TABRISI:12:42/r5.claim: An alternative takes the forgotten remembrance as the cupbearer's failure to mention Yusuf to the king; the author paraphrases this as Satan making him forget Yusuf before his master.

TABRISI:12:42/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، علي بن الحسين، أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:12:42/r6.claim: The stay of several years is specified as seven years in reports from Ibn Abbas, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, and Abu ʿAbd Allah.

TABRISI:12:42/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r7.speaker: رسول الله
TABRISI:12:42/r7.claim: A report from the Prophet marvels that Yusuf sought help from a creature instead of the Creator; another says his request to be remembered prolonged his stay.

TABRISI:12:42/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:12:42/r8.claim: In a report from Abu ʿAbd Allah, Gabriel asks Yusuf who gave him his beauty, his father's love, the caravan, rescue from the well, and protection from the women; Yusuf answers that God did, and is told to remain in prison for turning to a creature.

TABRISI:12:42/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:42/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:42/r9.claim: Seeking human help to avert harm is permitted and can even be required; the Prophet sought help from the Emigrants and Helpers, so the reports describe a temporary reproach for departing from Yusuf's usual reliance on God, not a prohibition.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r1.claim: The man Joseph thought would be saved was the cupbearer.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r10.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits a definition of biḍʿ as twelve years.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r11.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r11.claim: Ikrima defines biḍʿ as seven years.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r12.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r12.claim: Al-Hasan defines biḍʿ as between five and seven.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r13.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r13.claim: Mujahid defines biḍʿ as between four and nine.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r14.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r14.claim: Qatada defines biḍʿ as between three and nine, or ten.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r15.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r15.claim: Al-Farra says biḍʿ is below ten; al-Akhfash gives the range as one through ten.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r16.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r16.claim: Abu Ubayda says biḍʿ is less than a decade and half of it; Ibn Qutayba narrows it to one through four.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r17.speaker: أبو عبيدة عن الأثرم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r17.claim: A report from Abu Ubayda transmitted by al-Athram defines biḍʿ as between three and five.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r18.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r18.claim: The total prison stay is estimated as twelve years by Ibn Abbas, fourteen by al-Dahhak, or seven by Qatada.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r19.speaker: مالك بن دينار
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r19.claim: Malik ibn Dinar relates that God rebuked Joseph for taking the cupbearer as an intermediary and lengthened his imprisonment; Joseph wept that affliction had distracted his heart.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r3.claim: Qatada takes “thought” in its ordinary sense of belief short of certainty.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r4.claim: “Remember me with your master” means tell the king that a young man is imprisoned unjustly; the king was al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r5.claim: One view says Satan made the cupbearer forget to mention Joseph to the king.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq also assigns the forgetting to the cupbearer, who forgot Joseph before his master.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r7.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r7.claim: Mujahid, Muqatil, and al-Zajjaj instead say Satan made Joseph forget God and seek relief from the king; this was deliberate, not absentmindedness.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r8.claim: Joseph remained in prison additional years, as punishment for depending on a created person.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r9.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p227/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas's report to the Prophet explains biḍʿ as between seven and nine, in the story of Abu Bakr's wager over the Romans.

RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.claim: Joseph could infer that they served the king from their use of rabb for their master in the later statements about serving wine and asking to be remembered.

RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r1.claim: The referent of ظن is disputed: if Joseph, it may mean certain knowledge when his interpretation came by revelation, as in 2:46 and 69:20, or ordinary probability if he interpreted by learned principles.

RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r2.claim: Alternatively the survivor is the one who expected escape; since the two men did not believe Joseph's prophethood, his prediction gave them only an expectation.

RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r3.claim: Joseph asks the surviving cupbearer to mention to the king that he was wronged by his brothers, who sold him, and in the case for which he was imprisoned.

RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r4.claim: One interpretation says Satan made Joseph forget to remember God, faulting his reliance on a human instead of entrusting his need to God alone, as Abraham did when Gabriel offered help in the fire.

RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p115#2/r5.claim: On this reading, turning to the cupbearer let Satan gain influence and prolonged Joseph's trial in prison.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r1.claim: Al-Razi's own lifelong experience is that relying on others in affairs brings hardship, while relying on God's favor brings the desired result in the best way.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r2.claim: Some prefer the reading about the survivor forgetting Joseph because Satan's suggestion fits the survivor better and seeking help from people to escape injustice is lawful.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi prefers that Satan made Joseph forget God, appealing to the inner truths of worship; the verse's wording also weighs against the alternative, which would say Satan made him forget to mention Joseph to his lord.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r4.claim: Human help against injustice is permitted but spiritually imperfect for the most devoted; since God still praises Joseph and does not censure him for sexual wrongdoing, Joseph is innocent of the accusations made by ignorant traditionalists.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116#2/r5.claim: Satan can whisper suggestions but cannot erase knowledge from the heart; he can distract a person with other work so the knowledge is not recalled.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r1.claim: Critics say asking the king for help conflicts with Joseph's rejection of other gods; al-Razi clarifies that rabb here means human master, like master of a house or garment.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r2.claim: Joseph's earlier denial of all association with God makes reliance on a human appear inconsistent with total surrender to God.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r3.claim: Seeking people's help against oppression is legally allowed, but for the spiritual elect the better course is to detach from means and focus on the source of causes.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r4.claim: A second explanation says Joseph could properly ask the cupbearer but should have qualified the request by mentioning God, such as saying if God wills.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r5.claim: Another view makes the forgotten reminder the cupbearer's failure to mention Joseph to the king, which kept Joseph imprisoned; the author cites reports supporting blame for seeking a human intermediary.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r6.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r6.claim: A prophetic report says, May God have mercy on Joseph: had he not asked to be remembered by the king, he would not have remained in prison.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r7.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r7.claim: Qatada says Joseph was disciplined for turning to someone other than God.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r8.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r8.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi recounts that Joseph asked the prison companion to remember him before a lord other than the Lord Joseph had named.

RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r9.speaker: مالك
RAZI-FULL:v18p116/r9.claim: Malik reports that God reproached Joseph for appointing the cupbearer as an agent and would lengthen his imprisonment; Joseph wept and regretted the request.

RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r1.claim: Al-Razi explains that Satan can cause forgetfulness indirectly by distracting a person with other activity and preventing recall.

RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives bidʿ from cutting, making it a piece of a number; al-Farra says Arabs use it with tens from 10 to 90, implying three through nine.

RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r3.speaker: الشعبي
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi transmits a report in which the Prophet says bidʿ means less than ten.

RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r4.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r4.claim: Most commentators identify Joseph's bidʿ years as seven: he had spent five years in prison when he asked the cupbearer, then seven more.

RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph had nearly reached his release when he asked the cupbearer, but remained seven additional years.

RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v18p117/r6.claim: Al-Hasan transmits the report that Joseph's request caused the long imprisonment, then weeps and says people turn to other people when trouble comes.

RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p121/r6.claim: Joseph's refusal to answer the king immediately may have repaired his earlier reliance on the cupbearer: he focused on clearing his name instead of depending on the king's favor.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r1.claim: A report says a slave should not call someone my lord, but should say my master; the reason given is that Rabb is an agreed divine name while Sayyid's status as a divine name is disputed.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says this form of address may have been permitted under Joseph's law.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r3.claim: One reading takes the pronoun in فأنساه to mean Joseph: Satan made him forget God when he asked the cupbearer for help, so reliance on a creature brought a longer imprisonment.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r4.speaker: عبد العزيز بن عمير الكندي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r4.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Umayr al-Kindi tells that Gabriel rebuked Joseph for seeking a human's help, and God swore to keep him imprisoned for years; Joseph said he did not mind if God was pleased.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r5.claim: Another Gabriel story asks who saved Joseph from his brothers, the pit, sexual temptation, and women's schemes; Joseph answers God, then admits he trusted a creature and asks for mercy.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#2/r6.claim: Abu Salama reports the Prophet saying God have mercy on Joseph: without the request remember me before your master, Joseph would not have remained imprisoned for years.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet asked Abu Bakr how long bid' is; Abu Bakr answered three to seven, and the Prophet told him to raise the wager.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r10.speaker: مقاتل عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r10.claim: Maqatil, through Mujahid from Ibn Abbas, says Joseph remained five years and a bid' in prison.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r11.claim: Bid' derives from cutting: the penalty period was seven or nine years after five already passed, rather than the total time in prison.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r12.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r12.claim: Wahb says Joseph was jailed seven years, Job suffered seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was afflicted by transformation for seven years.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن راشد البصري
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r13.claim: Abdullah ibn Rashid al-Basri transmits from Sa'id ibn Abi Aruba that bid' is five to twelve years.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r14.claim: The verse permits using practical means despite certainty that outcomes belong to God, who arranged causes in a chain; forgetting is attributed to Satan as in Moses' encounter with al-Khidr.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r2.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r2.claim: Al-Tha'labi says most commentators define bid' as seven; al-Mawardi attributes that view to Abu Bakr and Qutrub.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد والأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r3.claim: Mujahid and al-Asma'i define bid' as three to nine.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas defines bid' as three to ten.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r5.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines bid' as three to five.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r6.claim: Al-Farra says bid' is used with tens from ten to ninety, but not after one hundred.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r7.speaker: ابن جريج وقتادة ووهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj, Qatada, and Wahb say Joseph spent seven years in prison; Wahb also says Job endured his trial for seven years.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph's imprisonment lasted twelve years.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r9.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42#3/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says the imprisonment lasted fourteen years.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r1.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r1.claim: Most commentators take ظن to mean certainty; Qatada instead reads it as conjecture because a dream interpreter only supposes, but the author prefers certainty as fitting the prophets and says Joseph's interpretation was revelation.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r2.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r2.claim: The phrase ربك means your master; al-A'sha's poem uses rabb for a generous master.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r3.claim: Joseph asked the cupbearer to tell the king his dream interpretation and that he was imprisoned unjustly.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r4.claim: A Muslim report from Abu Hurayra discourages saying feed, water, or wash your lord, and discourages calling people my lord or my slave; use master, mawla, or young man instead.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r5.claim: Quranic uses of rabb include this verse, a request to the master, and Joseph's statement that his master treated him well; rabb can also describe someone who manages and completes a matter.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r6.claim: Scholars understand the prophetic prohibition as advice to choose better wording, not a ban: other hadith and the Quran use rabb for a human master, but the clearer expression should be preferred.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r7.speaker: ابن شعبان
QURTUBI-FULL:12:42/r7.claim: Ibn Sha'ban says masters should not call people my slave and slaves should not call masters my lord or lady; the author explains the concern as divine servitude and the humiliation such labels cause.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r1.claim: A report says, May God have mercy on Joseph: but for asking the cupbearer to remember him before his master, he would not have remained in prison for years.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r10.claim: The author answers that 12:45 says the saved man later remembered; he adds that prophets can forget ordinary matters, though they are protected when conveying revelation, and scripture may attribute such forgetfulness to Satan.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r11.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying Adam forgot and his descendants forgot, and that he is human and forgets as others do.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r12.claim: Some interpreters say bid' means a span of time, pronounced with either a fatḥa or kasra, generally not combined with one hundred and extending up to ninety; al-Harawi defines it as three through nine, while Abu Ubayda's one through four is dismissed.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise says Joseph's request caused his long imprisonment and that remembering God would have secured his release.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r3.claim: A report from Yunus and al-Hasan attributes the same statement to the Prophet; al-Hasan then laments that people complain to others in hardship.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r4.claim: The alternative says the cupbearer, not Joseph, forgot to mention him; some prefer it because a person is not accountable for forgetfulness.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r5.claim: The author argues that 12:45 explicitly identifies the cupbearer as the one who remembered after a time; prophets are protected from forgetfulness only in delivering revelation, and may forget ordinary matters.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r6.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying Adam forgot and his descendants forgot, and that he himself forgets as other humans do.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph was punished with a prolonged imprisonment for telling the cupbearer to remember him; had he remembered God, he would have been freed.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r8.claim: Yunus reports al-Hasan quoting the Prophet that Joseph's words kept him in prison; al-Hasan wept and said people complain to others when hardship arrives.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:45/r9.claim: An alternative makes the pronoun refer to the cupbearer: Satan made him forget to mention Joseph to his master; some scholars prefer this because forgetfulness itself is not culpable.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r1.claim: If Joseph's expectation that one would be saved came from reasoning, it illustrates human effort; if from revelation, then 'thought' means certain knowledge.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r2.claim: Joseph asked the saved cupbearer to mention his situation to the king so that he could be released.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r3.claim: The pronoun in 'Satan made him forget' may refer to the cupbearer, whom Satan made forget to mention Joseph; the source can be attributed through association or refer to mentioning the Lord's affairs.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r4.claim: Alternatively, Satan made Joseph forget God by seeking help from someone else; a prophetic saying supports this by saying that without the request Joseph would not have remained seven years after the first five.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r5.claim: A prophetic report says, 'May God have mercy on my brother Joseph'; had he not asked the cupbearer to mention him, he would not have remained in prison seven years after the five already served.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:42/r6.claim: Seeking people's help in hardship is generally acceptable but does not suit the station of prophets; bid' means a span from three to nine and comes from cutting.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r1.claim: If the interpretation came through reasoning, Joseph was the one who thought the cupbearer would be saved; if by revelation, the cupbearer was the one who thought so; alternatively, ẓanna means certainty.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r2.claim: Joseph asks the cupbearer to describe him and his case to the king in hope of release from his predicament.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r3.claim: Satan made the cupbearer forget to mention Joseph to the king, or made Joseph forget God when he entrusted his affair to another.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#2/r4.claim: A prophetic report says God have mercy on Joseph: had he not asked the cupbearer to remember him, he would not have remained in prison seven years; most say the years were seven, while biḍʿ means three through nine.

QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r1.claim: Asking the cupbearer to remember him means seeking stable spiritual existence through love; intoxicated love raises spirit to unity and heart to spirit, but both remain veiled in divine light rather than annihilated.

QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r2.claim: Remaining at that level can produce ego and transgression; Satanic illusion makes Joseph forget annihilation because he seeks the spirit's station and retains a remainder of self.

QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r3.speaker: عليه السلام
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r3.claim: A prophetic report says God have mercy on Joseph: had he not asked the cupbearer to remember him, he would not have remained imprisoned for years.

QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, illusion forgets the love-messenger when love dominates in bewildered witnessing; the lover forgets creation and self in unity until annihilation ends and divine life restores differentiation.

QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:41-42#2/r5.claim: The prison's duration is the spiritual journey; the later visions of cattle and grain symbolize changes in soul and bodily qualities during seclusion and return.

QASHANI:12:41-42/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:41-42/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:41-42/r4.claim: When both faculties function through God rather than themselves, confinement ends and subsistence begins, though a trace of ego remains.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r1.claim: Qatāda takes ẓann in its ordinary sense because dream interpretation is conjectural.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes Joseph the one who thought the cupbearer would be released; Abū Ḥayyān says this is difficult if the interpretation came by conjecture because the decree is final, unless the phrase only means Joseph has finished speaking.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r3.claim: Joseph may have asked the cupbearer to tell the king about his knowledge and standing, or to report his unjust imprisonment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān sees Joseph's request as permissible practical help, with God making it a cause of relief; he compares it to Jesus seeking helpers and the Prophet seeking a guard.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers that Joseph wanted to lead the cupbearer to faith, as he had sought the guidance of both prisoners.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r6.claim: The pronoun in فأنساه refers to the cupbearer; ذكر ربه means remembering Joseph for his master, and the loose relation permits the possessive.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r7.claim: Satan's whisper distracted the cupbearer until he forgot Joseph's request; God prolonged Joseph's imprisonment to increase his reward.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r8.claim: A few years is left vague; reports give seven or twelve, or count seven after the prisoners left or two years, while the apparent sense is Joseph's full prison term.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r9.claim: Some make the pronoun in أنساه refer to Joseph and build stories on that reading that Abū Ḥayyān says should not be attributed to prophets.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r1.claim: بضع سنين is a temporal adverb, and authorities give different ranges for بضع.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r2.claim: Qatada says بضع covers three through nine.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r3.claim: Abu Ubayd says بضع is below ten and below half a decade? He gives its range as one to ten.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r4.claim: Mujahid defines بضع as three through seven.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ says بضع is used with tens, not with one hundred or one thousand.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r6.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r6.claim: Al-Raghib derives بضع from a cut-off part of ten and gives the ranges three to ten or above five and below ten.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:42#2/r7.claim: The word is linked to cutting: بضع اللحم means cut meat, بضاعة is a piece of capital, and مبضع is the cutting tool; بعض was discussed under البعوضة.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r1.claim: ظن may be attributed to Joseph if his dream interpretation was reasoning, or to the cupbearer if the interpretation came by revelation; it may also mean certainty.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r2.claim: If ظن retains its ordinary sense, it suits Joseph only under independent reasoning; revelation is certain and would make the cupbearer the one who thought, unless ظن means certainty.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r3.speaker: قتادة
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r3.claim: Qatada keeps the ordinary sense of ظن and attributes it to Joseph because dream interpretation is conjectural.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r4.claim: منهما may modify ناج or be a circumstantial phrase from the relative pronoun; attaching it to ناج would misleadingly suggest someone escaped from the two.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa rejects attaching منهما to ناج because that is not the intended sense.

SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:42/r6.claim: The pronoun in فأنساه refers to the cupbearer; the alternative reference to Joseph is weak.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r1.claim: Yusuf privately asks the surviving cupbearer to mention his case to the king, apparently so the other prisoner will not realize he is to be crucified.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r2.claim: The cupbearer forgot to speak to the king, which Ibn Kathir calls one of Satan's stratagems to keep God's prophet imprisoned.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r3.claim: The pronoun in 'Satan made him forget' correctly refers to the rescued cupbearer, as Mujahid, Ibn Ishaq, and others held.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r4.claim: An alternative, transmitted by Ibn Jarir from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrima, and others, makes the pronoun refer to Yusuf.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Yusuf's request for relief from someone other than God prolonged his imprisonment; Ibn Kathir calls it very weak because Sufyan ibn Waki and Ibrahim al-Khuzi are both weak, the latter weaker.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r6.claim: Mursal versions from al-Hasan and Qatada are also unacceptable here, even if mursal reports are accepted in other contexts.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r7.claim: Mujahid and Qatada define bid' as a span from three to nine years.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r8.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r8.claim: Wahb says Ayyub endured affliction seven years, Yusuf remained in prison seven, and Nebuchadnezzar's punishment lasted seven.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r9.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p391/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that Yusuf remained twelve years, and separately says fourteen years.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r8.claim: ظن may mean knowledge, since all human knowledge is nothing beside God's, or ordinary inference from clues; this could permit decisive speech based on probability, or the subject may be the cupbearer.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r9.claim: Joseph asks the cupbearer to tell the king about Joseph's virtue and clean character, which contradict the accusation against him; رب here means the king, unlike God's use elsewhere.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r2.claim: As Joseph predicted, the cupbearer survived and the baker was crucified; Satan made the cupbearer forget Joseph because Joseph relied on him, prolonging Joseph's imprisonment.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r3.claim: Joseph's continued imprisonment teaches that causes have no effect independently of God; بضع means three through nine, and the reported term here was seven years.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r4.speaker: التوراة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r4.claim: The Torah account says Midianites brought Joseph to Egypt and Potiphar bought him; God prospered his work, and Potiphar trusted him with his household and possessions.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r5.speaker: التوراة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r5.claim: In the Torah account, Joseph refuses his master's wife as betrayal and sin before God, flees when she seizes his tunic, and she falsely accuses him of attempted assault.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r6.speaker: التوراة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p44/r6.claim: The Torah says Potiphar imprisoned Joseph, but God won him favor with the jailer, who entrusted him with the prisoners; whatever Joseph did prospered.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r1.speaker: التوراة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r1.claim: The Torah says Pharaoh jailed his cupbearer and baker in Joseph's prison after they offended him, and Joseph served them; they had separate dreams on the same night.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r2.speaker: التوراة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r2.claim: In the cupbearer's dream, a vine had three branches that budded, flowered, and ripened into grapes; he squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup and served the king.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r3.speaker: التوراة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r3.claim: Joseph interprets the three branches as three days, after which Pharaoh will restore the cupbearer; he asks him to remember Joseph and help free him.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r4.speaker: التوراة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r4.claim: The baker dreams of three baskets of bread on his head, with birds eating the uppermost food; Joseph interprets the baskets as three days before the baker is executed and eaten by birds.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r5.speaker: التوراة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p45/r5.claim: On Pharaoh's birthday, the cupbearer was restored and the baker executed as Joseph predicted, but the cupbearer did not remember Joseph.

DURR-FULL:v4p534/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p534/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p534/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas describes three punishments for Joseph: prison over his desire, prolonged prison after asking the cupbearer to remember him, and the brothers' taunt that Benjamin had stolen as Joseph accused them of theft.

DURR-FULL:v4p540/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r5.speaker: ابن سابط
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r5.claim: Ibn Sabit explains Joseph's request to be remembered before the cupbearer's lord as a request to be remembered before the king; Qatadah gives the same gloss.

DURR-FULL:v4p540/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r6.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r6.claim: On the way to prison, Joseph told the guard who asked his need that he wanted the man to mention him to his lord, meaning the king who ruled Joseph.

DURR-FULL:v4p540/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r7.claim: Qatadah says dream interpretation proceeds by conjecture, while God may confirm or undo what He wills.

DURR-FULL:v4p540/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r8.claim: A report from the Prophet says that, had Joseph not uttered his request to the cupbearer, he would not have remained in prison so long; the report connects this to seeking relief from someone besides God.

DURR-FULL:v4p540/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet's prayer for mercy on Joseph and says he would have left prison quickly instead of asking the cupbearer to remember him.

DURR-FULL:v4p541/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r1.claim: Hasan transmits a Prophetic prayer for mercy on Joseph because he asked the cupbearer to remember him; Hasan weeps and says people turn to other people when hardship comes.

DURR-FULL:v4p541/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r2.claim: Qatadah says a report from the Prophet blamed Joseph's seeking another's intercession, and that he was punished for seeking an intermediary against his Lord.

DURR-FULL:v4p541/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r3.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r3.claim: In a report from Anas, God asks Joseph who rescued him from his brothers, the well, and the woman; Joseph answers God, then explains that distress made him utter a word and remember a human.

DURR-FULL:v4p541/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r4.claim: Hasan reports that God asked Joseph whether he had taken a human as an agent and threatened longer confinement; Joseph wept that distress had occupied his heart.

DURR-FULL:v4p541/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r5.claim: Mujahid says Joseph asked the surviving prisoner to mention him to the king; Satan made the cupbearer forget, and Joseph was punished for seeking release through the king.

DURR-FULL:v4p541/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p541/r6.claim: Qatadah says reports reached them that Joseph remained in prison for seven years.

DURR-FULL:v4p542/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r1.claim: Wahb says Job suffered for seven years, Joseph remained in prison for seven, and Nebuchadnezzar was tormented among beasts for seven.

DURR-FULL:v4p542/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph remained imprisoned for twelve years.

DURR-FULL:v4p542/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r3.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says Joseph's one word caused seven years' imprisonment; Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash adds that he had already been imprisoned for five years.

DURR-FULL:v4p542/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r4.speaker: طاوس والضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r4.claim: Tawus and al-Dahhak say Joseph remained imprisoned for fourteen years.

DURR-FULL:v4p542/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r5.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r5.claim: Mujahid and Qatadah define biḍʿ as a period of three to nine years; Ibn Abbas says it is less than ten.

DURR-FULL:v4p542/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas counts three lapses by Joseph: asking to be remembered, accusing his brothers of theft, and saying he had not betrayed the Aziz; Gabriel mentioned Joseph's desire, and he answered that he did not absolve himself.

DURR-FULL:v4p542/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r7.speaker: قتادة
